1) Background / Context

BookStack is a self-hosted, user-friendly platform designed for organizing and storing documentation. It simplifies document management by offering a structured hierarchy similar to a stack of books, where users can create books, chapters, and pages. This intuitive design aims to facilitate easy information retrieval and documentation creation.

2) Objectives

The primary objective is to provide users with a simple, out-of-the-box documentation platform that enhances information organization and accessibility. The system is designed to enable seamless documentation creation, management, and retrieval, while also ensuring secure access control.

3) Stakeholders & Users

- Primary Users: Documentation authors and administrators.
- Stakeholders: Organizations or individuals seeking an efficient self-hosted documentation solution.

4) Functional Descriptions

- Book and Page Structure: Users can create hierarchical documentation by organizing content into books, chapters, and pages.
- Bookshelves: Multiple books can be grouped into bookshelves to organize topics further.
- Search and Linking: A powerful search feature allows searching across books, chapters, and pages. Users can link directly to specific paragraphs.
- Content Management: Includes cross-book sorting, page revisions, and image management.
- Access Control: A role and permission system limits content visibility and user actions. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is supported.
- API and Tokens: Support for API tokens to integrate with external systems.
- Comments and Tags: Users can comment on content and tag entities for better categorization.

5) Non-Functional Descriptions

- Usability: Designed for ease of use with a focus on intuitive navigation and basic word-processing proficiency.
- Security: Incorporates robust security measures, including MFA and permissions.
- Performance: Optimized for efficient search and content retrieval.
- Scalability: Capable of handling increased documentation and user load as organizations grow.

-- Schema for database: schemabench_0015
CREATE TABLE `books` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `title` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `description` text,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bookshelves` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `title` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `description` text,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bookshelf_books` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `bookshelf_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `book_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `bookshelf_id` (`bookshelf_id`),
  KEY `book_id` (`book_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bookshelf_books_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`bookshelf_id`) REFERENCES `bookshelves` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `bookshelf_books_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`book_id`) REFERENCES `books` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `chapters` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `title` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `description` text,
  `book_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `book_id` (`book_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `chapters_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`book_id`) REFERENCES `books` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `page_versions` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `page_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `version` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `content` text,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `page_id` (`page_id`),
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `pages` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `title` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `content` text,
  `chapter_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `chapter_id` (`chapter_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `pages_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`chapter_id`) REFERENCES `chapters` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `users` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `username` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `email` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `password` char(60) NOT NULL,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `email` (`email`),
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `user_roles` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `role` enum('admin','author','reader') NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `user_id` (`user_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `user_roles_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `book_comments` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `book_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `comment` text,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `book_id` (`book_id`),
  KEY `user_id` (`user_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `book_comments_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`book_id`) REFERENCES `books` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `book_comments_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `page_comments` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `page_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `comment` text,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `page_id` (`page_id`),
  KEY `user_id` (`user_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `page_comments_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`page_id`) REFERENCES `pages` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `page_comments_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `tags` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `page_tags` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `page_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `tag_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `page_id` (`page_id`),
  KEY `tag_id` (`tag_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `page_tags_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`page_id`) REFERENCES `pages` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `page_tags_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`tag_id`) REFERENCES `tags` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `api_tokens` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `token` char(255) NOT NULL,
  `expires_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `user_id` (`user_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `api_tokens_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
